title: Reverend Beckton and When the Saints Go Marching In
summary: An evangelist, Reverend Beckton, travelled with a jazz band and popularised The Saints around 1926, and was later murdered in Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: "A Closer Walk." That didn't effect me as "The Saints" did. But there was a guy that really started "The Saints", really started that song to be very popular as a Jazz song, and he was an (you know, what do you call the guys who get...?) evangelist. And he came to my home town. His name was Reverend Beckon. And he used to have a Jazz group that went with him. And they used to play "When The Saints Go Marching In." And that's when the people really started catching on to "When The Saints Go Marching In." Around '24 or '25...no, about '26, I would think. His name was Reverend Beckton. In fact, he got murdered in Philadelphia by gangsters or something.
How did you spell his last name?

Beckton. He's the first one that I can recall (I mean, in this part of the country) who started that on "When The Saints Go Marching In", rolling(?)... He had a Jazz band with him, that traveled with him. He was an evangelist, like Billy Graham. I think Billy Graham has got a band...
He's got Ethel Waters. He had her for a long time.
Which is quite something to have. I don't know how she sounds now, but...
I think he's got a band with him, too, hasn't he?
Yeah, well, he must have. He's got the singers, something to back him up.
Did this Reverend Beckton travel all over the country?
He traveled around, too, yeah. Then he got to be in Philadelphia for a little while, and that's where he met his end.
He must have been on to something good.
